Figma Builds In-House Redis Proxy to Hit Six Nines Uptime
Articles
·
InfoQ
·
Today
90

Figma has published a detailed engineering post on building FigCache, an in-house Redis proxy service that replaced a fragmented caching stack. The system, in production since mid-2025, has achieved six nines of uptime. The project was motivated by connection volume limits, thundering herd issues, and a sprawl of client libraries with inconsistent observability. Figma chose to build a custom proxy rather than adopt existing open-source solutions due to the need for semantic awareness of Redis commands and support for a fragmented client base. FigCache is a stateless Go service built on a custom RPC framework (ResPC) over the Redis Serialization Protocol (RESP). Its architecture separates a frontend layer for connection management from a backend layer for command execution. A notable design choice is using a Starlark program evaluated at runtime to generate the backend configuration, allowing routing logic changes without redeployment. The proxy also handles multi-shard pipelines internally, eliminating CROSSSLOT errors. Migration was designed to be reversible at every stage, with feature flags and incremental traffic shifts. The system has eliminated thundering herd failures, made shard failovers and hardware rotations zero-downtime operations, and unified observability across the caching stack.

Cloudflare Introduces Flagship: an Edge-Native Feature Flag Service Built on OpenFeature
Articles
·
InfoQ
·
Today
87

Cloudflare has announced the closed beta of Flagship, a new feature flag service deeply integrated into its global edge platform. Built on the CNCF open standard OpenFeature, Flagship allows developers to control feature rollouts and run experiments without redeploying code. Its key differentiator is native evaluation within Cloudflare Workers via a binding, eliminating network round-trips to external services like LaunchDarkly and achieving sub-millisecond latency. Flagship supports boolean, string, number, and JSON flag values, along with priority-based targeting rules and percentage-based rollouts. The service is particularly relevant for AI-driven and agent-based workloads requiring rapid iteration and low latency. Industry commentators view this as a sign that feature flags are becoming commoditized infrastructure, with major platforms offering native solutions. A browser client provider for prefetching and caching flags is also available. Flagship is currently in closed beta.
